newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Mogul Murdoch to guide son in Australia.
newsitem.headline: Mogul Murdoch to guide son in Australia.

text.p: Lachlan Murdoch, the eldest son of global media baron Rupert Murdoch, was now favoured over his sister Elisabeth to eventually take control of the News Corp Ltd empire, analysts said on Tuesday.

The analysts told Reuters the earlier announced appointment of 25-year-old Lachlan as the boss of the company's Australian operations cemented his favouritism -- once Rupert Murdoch decided the time was right to step aside.
"You would have to say Lachlan is the favoured one at this time," said a local media analyst who asked not to be named.
"He is the only one on the board (of News Corp)," the analysts said

Rupert Murdoch said in a statement from Los Angeles that Lachlan would assume responsibility for the Australian operations with the retirement of News Ltd executive chairman Ken Cowley in June this year.
"I think Ken has been backing out for a while," said the head of an institutional dealing desk at one large European-owned broker.

He and others said the appointment meant little for the share price of News Corp, which has languished in recent months due to doubts over the company's ability to meet its bullish annual profit forecast.
"The stock has been a fairly lousy performer of late. It is a bit better today but certainly it is not a reaction to today's announcement," the dealer said.
News Corp shares were 11 cents higher at A$5.83 at 3.25 p.m. (0525 GMT) on Tuesday.
Most analysts doubted if Lachlan Murdoch, educated in the United States with only three years experience in Australia, would make any key decisions without reference to a higher authority.

"Who do you think is really running it? It is the same thing with James Packer (the son of local media billionaire Kerry Packer who is managing director of the listed Publishing and Broadcasting Ltd )," said another analyst.
"I would be flabbergasted if either of them were in a position to make a decision off their own bat without having to get it through appropriate people."
Two other analysts, neither of whom would be named, were little fussed by Lachlan Murdoch's youth.
One said Lachlan might take a more competitive marketing and sales position than Cowley did against metropolitan newspaper rival John Fairfax Holdings Ltd.

"You will have harder pressure on Fairfax but I think Lachlan is going to get dragged up into the family activities internationally rather than Australia only," said one, who expected Lachlan to stay in Australia at most for another three years.
Another analyst said at this stage of his career Lachlan was older than his father was when he took control of his first newspaper, the Adelaide News.
"How old was his dad when he took over?? -- 21. That is the question that everyone is going to be asking," the analyst said.
Elisabeth, 28, is a marketing executive with the News Corp affiliate British Sky Broadcasting Plc in London.
For the past year, most local and overseas analysts have speculated that the succession stakes would be fought out between Lachlan and Elisabeth.
Lachlan, however, appeared to gain the upper hand in September last year when he became managing director of the Australian offshoot News Ltd and one month later joined the board of News Corp.
They probably have some time to wait before the speculation is anything other than just that.
For his part, Rupert Murdoch, who is now 66, has not said when he plans to retire, step aside, or disappear from the company which he founded more than 30 years ago.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
